## Answer: about $6,748 of the $7,000 conversion is taxable income for 2025

Luka put a nondeductible $7,000 contribution into traditional IRA SYN-12040003 on 10 Feb 2025. Three days later he converted $7,000 to his Roth IRA, SYN-12040004. A backdoor conversion is only tax-free if he has no other pre-tax IRA money. But his rollover IRA, SYN-12040002, stayed open as planned in December 2024, and it was worth **$187,544.92 on 31 Dec 2025**.

The pro-rata rule treats all his traditional IRAs as one pot, valued at year end. His $7,000 of after-tax money is only a small slice of that pot. So only that slice of the conversion comes out tax-free.

**Form 8606, 2025:**

| Line | Item | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Nondeductible contribution for 2025 | $7,000.00 |
| 2 | Basis from earlier years (tax profile, as of 31 Dec 2024) | $0.00 |
| 3 | Total basis | $7,000.00 |
| 6 | Traditional IRAs on 31 Dec 2025 (SYN-12040002: $42,871.51 + $142,362.18 + $2,311.23 cash; SYN-12040003: $0) | $187,544.92 |
| 8 | Amount converted | $7,000.00 |
| 9 | Line 6 + line 8 | $194,544.92 |
| 10 | Tax-free share (line 3 ÷ line 9) | 0.03598 |
| 11 / 13 | Tax-free part of the conversion | $251.87 |
| **18** | **Taxable part of the conversion** | **$6,748.13** (≈ $6,748) |
| **14** | **Basis carried to 2026** | **$6,748.13** |

The 1099-R shows the full $7,000 as taxable, but its "taxable amount not determined" box is checked. The real taxable amount comes from Form 8606. It isn't $0, and it isn't the full $7,000. The basis isn't lost: $6,748.13 carries forward and will come out tax-free on later conversions or withdrawals.

**Caveats:**
- I've treated the contribution as nondeductible for 2025, as the December 2024 plan says. The W-2s don't show whether either of them has a workplace retirement plan, so the preparer should confirm it is reported on Form 8606 and not deducted.
- The 2025 return is due today. The preparer needs these figures now, or should file an extension.

Then record the follow-up in the CRM, for this household only, dated 15 April 2026: a note of what was discussed and decided, with the figures it turns on, and an activity for each item someone still has to do. Then draft the client's message.

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "pro_rata_tax" if part of the conversion is taxable under the pro-rata rule, "no_pro_rata_tax" if none of it is, or "unresolved"

- "basis_carried": the basis in traditional IRAs carried to 2026 (Form 8606 line 14), or null if unresolved
- "figures": every figure you relied on, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed rather than read

- "client_message": the message to the client, as plain text
